question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus assigning a 95% probability that Xi Jinping remains in office through the end of 2026 stems from his consolidated authority within the Chinese Communist Party after the 20th National Congress and the absence of visible factional challenges or succession signals ahead of the 2027 party congress. Loyalist appointments in the Politburo and military, combined with institutional controls, have limited openings for internal opposition. No confirmed leadership disputes or health developments have surfaced in recent months to shift these assessments. Realistic factors that could still move probabilities include sudden medical events, elite power realignments, or major policy crises prompting collective action, though current indicators show limited precedent for rapid change before the scheduled leadership transition window.

eventMetadata.context_description: The 2028 Democratic presidential nomination remains wide open more than two years before primaries, with no major candidate declarations and a fragmented field of governors, senators, House members, and former officials keeping implied probabilities clustered near the top. Trader consensus reflected on Polymarket shows Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez edging ahead at roughly 21 percent, followed closely by Jon Ossoff and Gavin Newsom, as national polls often favor Kamala Harris while early-state surveys and market pricing highlight rising support for younger or more progressive figures. Recent gains for Ocasio-Cortez and Ossoff track summer polling shifts and speculation around 2026 midterm performance, while Newsom’s earlier lead has moderated. The DNC’s proposed calendar keeping South Carolina first could also shape early dynamics. Outcomes hinge on midterm results, eventual candidate entries, fundraising, and primary-state polling that have yet to produce clear separation.
